title: Verifying Signatures
description: Verify GPG and SSH signatures on commits and tags, and enforce signature requirements in your repository.

data.text: Verifying signatures ensures that commits and tags were created by the claimed author and have not been modified since. Git provides built-in verification for both GPG and SSH signatures, and platforms like GitHub display verification status in their web UIs.
Use git log --show-signature to verify GPG signatures on commits. Use git tag -v to verify signed tags. Git checks the signature against the GPG keys in your keyring.

data.title: Verify GPG signatures on commits
data.code:
# Show signature status for the last 5 commits
git log --show-signature -5

# Verify a specific commit
git log --show-signature -1 abc1234

# Output for a verified commit:
# gpg: Signature made ... using RSA key ID ABCDEF12
# gpg: Good signature from "Your Name <your-email@example.com>"

# Output for an unverified commit:
# gpg: Signature made ... using RSA key ID ABCDEF12
# gpg: Can't check signature: No public key

# Import the missing public key to verify:
gpg --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com --recv-keys ABCDEF12

data.text: Git 2.34+ supports SSH-based signing. Use git log --show-signature to verify SSH signatures. Git checks the signature against the public key stored in the commit metadata.

data.title: Verify SSH signatures
data.code:
# Configure Git for SSH signing
git config --global gpg.format ssh
git config --global user.signingkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

# Show signature status
git log --show-signature -1 HEAD

# Output for SSH-signed commit:
# gpg: Signature made ... using RSA key ID SHA256:abc123...
# gpg: Good signature from "Your Name (ssh key) <your-email@example.com>"

data.text: Signed tags verify the authenticity of a release. Use git tag -v for GPG-signed tags and git verify-tag for SSH-signed tags.

data.title: Verify signed tags
data.code:
# Verify a GPG-signed tag
git tag -v v2.1.0

# Verify an SSH-signed tag
git verify-tag v2.1.0

# Output for a verified tag:
# gpg: Signature made ... using RSA key ID ABCDEF12
# gpg: Good signature from "Your Name <your-email@example.com>"
# object abc1234...
# type commit
# tag v2.1.0

data.text: You can enforce signed commits using a server-side pre-receive hook. This hook rejects pushes that contain unsigned commits. GitHub does not enforce this by default for public repositories; use GitHub Enterprise or a self-hosted Git server for enforcement.

data.title: Server-side pre-receive hook to enforce signed commits
data.code:
# /opt/git/project.git/hooks/pre-receive
#!/bin/bash

while read oldrev newrev refname; do
  # Get commits being pushed
  for commit in $(git rev-list $oldrev..$newrev); do
    # Check if commit is signed
git verify-commit $commit >/dev/null 2>&1
    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
      echo "ERROR: Commit $commit is not signed"
      exit 1
    fi
  done
done

exit 0

# Make the hook executable
chmod +x /opt/git/project.git/hooks/pre-receive

data.title: GitHub does not enforce signed commits for public repos
data.text: GitHub displays verification status but does not block unsigned pushes for public repositories. Use GitHub Enterprise or a self-hosted Git server with pre-receive hooks if you need enforcement.
In CI, verify that all commits in the build are signed. This ensures the build was triggered by a trusted developer and not by a compromised account or unauthorized bot.

data.title: Verify signatures in GitHub Actions
data.code:
# .github/workflows/verify-sigs.yml
- run: |
    # Import the GPG public key
    echo "$GPG_PUBLIC_KEY" | gpg --import -

    # Verify all commits in the push
git rev-list --no-merges ${{ github.event.before }}..${{ github.sha }} | \
  while read commit; do
    git verify-commit $commit || exit 1
  done
  env:
    GPG_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ secrets.GPG_PUBLIC_KEY }}

items.question: Can I verify a signature if I do not have the public key?
items.answer: No. Import the signer's public key from a keyserver (gpg --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com --recv-keys <key-id>) or ask the signer to share it directly.

items.question: What if verification shows 'expired'?
items.answer: The signing key has expired. Ask the signer to extend the expiration or create a new key. Expired keys still verify the commit's authenticity at the time of signing.

items.question: Can I require signed tags for releases?
items.answer: Yes. Use a server-side hook to reject unsigned tags, or require manual verification during the release process.

items.question: Does git verify-commit check the commit message?
items.answer: No. It checks the cryptographic signature only. The commit message and content are protected by the signature's hash.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: git log --show-signature verifies GPG and SSH signatures on commits
Import the signer's public key to verify their commits
Use server-side pre-receive hooks to enforce signed commits
Verify signatures in CI to ensure builds come from trusted developers
